text.p: UK pharmaceuticals giant Smithkline Beecham Plc plans to spin off some of its technology into a new biotechnology company, said a report in the Financial Times on Friday.
The report said the group was taking the unusual step of handing over a number of its patents and laboratory equipment in return for a 10 percent stake in the company called Adprotech.
The report said the company will get around five million in cash from venture capital groups. The spin-off will be led by Dr Janet Dewdney, retired director of Smithkline's biotechnology unit.

Adprotech's patents cover proteins called complements which are involved in immune systems and the company hopes to develop treatments for conditions including strokes, multiple sclerosis and heart disease, said the FT.
